study_material.title: Day Sequence / Calendar - Complete Study Notes
study_material.introduction: Calendar questions ask for the day of the week after some interval, or which years share a calendar. Everything runs on 'odd days' - the remainder of days modulo 7.
learning_objectives: Compute odd days for spans of days, months and years
Identify leap years including century rules
Find the day of the week after a given gap
Reason about repeated calendars and same-day dates

concepts.heading: 1. Odd Days
concepts.body: Odd days = total days mod 7. If today is Monday, 61 days later is 61 mod 7 = 5 odd days ahead: Saturday. All calendar arithmetic reduces to counting odd days.

concepts.heading: 2. Leap Years
concepts.body: A year is leap if divisible by 4 - EXCEPT centuries, which must be divisible by 400. So 2024 and 2000 are leap; 1900 and 2100 are not. A leap year has 366 days = 2 odd days; an ordinary year has 365 = 1 odd day.

concepts.heading: 3. Month Odd Days
concepts.body: Jan 3, Feb 0 (or 1 in leap year), Mar 3, Apr 2, May 3, Jun 2, Jul 3, Aug 3, Sep 2, Oct 3, Nov 2, Dec 3. Summing month odd days lets you walk from a known date to any other in the year.

concepts.heading: 4. Next Year Same Date
concepts.body: The same date next year moves forward 1 weekday after an ordinary year, 2 after a leap year (if the span crosses Feb 29). Jan 1 2024 (Monday, leap year) makes Jan 1 2025 a Wednesday.

concepts.heading: 5. Reference Facts
concepts.body: 15 August 1947 was a Friday. 1 January 2000 was a Saturday. Centuries: 100 years contain 5 odd days, 200 years 3, 300 years 1, 400 years 0 - so the calendar repeats every 400 years.

formulas: Ordinary year = 1 odd day; leap year = 2
shortcut_methods: Only track remainders mod 7 - never total days
Count leap years in a span as floor(n/4) with century corrections
Same weekday shifts +1 per ordinary year, +2 per leap year crossed
common_mistakes: Forgetting Feb 29 only matters if the span crosses it
Adding days instead of odd days for long spans
study_material.summary: Reduce everything modulo 7, know the leap rule (including centuries), and use +1/+2 shifts for year-to-year questions.
quick_revision_notes: Same date next year: +1 (+2 across Feb 29)

solved_examples.question: If today is Monday, what day will it be after 61 days?
Which of these is a leap year?
solved_examples.step_by_step: Centuries must be divisible by 400: only 2000 qualifies.

solved_examples.question: 1 January 2024 was a Monday. What day was 1 January 2025?
solved_examples.step_by_step: 2024 is leap (366 days = 2 odd days): Monday + 2 = Wednesday.
solved_examples.shortcut: Leap year shifts the next year by 2 days.

solved_examples.question: How many odd days are there in 100 years?
solved_examples.step_by_step: 76 ordinary (76 odd) + 24 leap (48 odd) = 124 odd days = 124 mod 7 = 5.

practice_questions.question: If today is Friday, what day is it after 45 days?
How many days does February have in a leap year?
Which year is NOT a leap year?
practice_questions.explanation: 1900/400 is not whole; century years need division by 400.

practice_questions.question: 15 August 2023 was a Tuesday. What day was 15 August 2024?
practice_questions.explanation: The span crosses Feb 29 2024: shift +2, Tuesday to Thursday.

practice_questions.question: If the day before yesterday was Thursday, what day will it be the day after tomorrow?
practice_questions.explanation: Today is Saturday; day after tomorrow is Monday.

practice_questions.question: What is the probability that an ordinary (non-leap) year has 53 Sundays?
practice_questions.explanation: One extra day beyond 52 weeks; it is a Sunday with probability 1/7.
